The Independent — datePublished and dateModified both 2026-10-25T17:04:05Z = 17:04 GMT Sun 25 Oct (after the cutover, so Z = local). Retrieved by curl at 17:35 GMT.

LEAD: "A man has been killed by a falling tree and hundreds of thousands of homes have been left without power as Storm Boelo battered the country with gusts reaching 84mph."

THE DEATH — THIRD APPROVED SOURCE
"A 60-year-old man was killed by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, with police called to the scene at around 10:30am on Sunday morning. The man was pronounced dead at the scene, Police Scotland said."

POWER — ENA FIGURES, WITH A DIFFERENT TIME ATTRIBUTION
"The storm caused widespread power cuts in Scotland and England's north west. Engineers have reconnected 344,900 customers to power but 82,600 were disconnected on Sunday AFTERNOON, the Energy Networks Association said."
The same two numbers are attributed by BBC (12:37 GMT) and the Guardian (17:10 GMT) to ENA "on Sunday MORNING". See the conflict note below.

GUSTS — PA-STYLE MET OFFICE SET
"Sunday began with heavy winds in northern parts of the UK - widely reaching 60 to 70mph and at 84mph in Argyll and Bute, 83mph in Snowdonia and 82mph in the Inner Hebrides, the Met Office said."

WARNING TIMING
"A Met Office amber weather warning for wind remains in place for Scotland and much of northern England until 9pm, having been activated at 9pm on Saturday."

FLOODING
"The Environment Agency had issued six warnings that flooding is expected for spots in northern parts of England, as well as 50 other alerts where it is possible. The Scottish Environment Protection Agency said 17 flood warnings and 11 flooding alerts were active on Sunday afternoon."

FERRIES AND FLIGHTS
"Of CalMac's 30 services, 24 have been cancelled, some of them until Monday."
Stena Line cancelled Belfast to Liverpool and Cairnryan; Western Ferries suspended; DFDS cancelled Dover-Calais crossings.
"Some 17 flights at Belfast international were cancelled by Sunday lunchtime, while some services were diverted from landing at Leeds Bradford Airport and others were cancelled."
Leeds Bradford spokesperson, quoted: "We appreciate that this is a challenging situation. Our teams are working in very difficult conditions to support passengers as best they can."

RAIL
Network Rail Scotland: flooding at Dalmarnock station in Glasgow submerged the tracks between the platforms overnight and "overwhelming its water pumps for a time"; the station is now clear but the line is closed between Partick and Rutherglen for planned engineering work. A fallen tree blocked a line between Liverpool and Manchester.

LOCAL DETAIL
A business in Largs, North Ayrshire, which posted video of the flooding claimed the street flooded "at its highest level ever".

DO NOT CONFLATE — SEPARATE SCOTTISH DEATH REPORTED TODAY
Independent, https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/jim-wither-arran-ferry-search-b3072984.html, 2026-10-25T15:44:02Z = 15:44 GMT: a body found on a Largs beach is believed to be Jim Wither, 82, of Johnstone, Renfrewshire, who went overboard from the MV Caledonian Isles near Arran at about 20:30 on Sunday 18 October, a WEEK before Storm Boelo. Police Scotland say the death is not suspicious. This is NOT a Storm Boelo casualty and must not be added to a Boelo toll.
